answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging each identity a real, non-refundable cost before it can transact — like a harbor that only lets a ship dock after it has hauled cargo to the wharf. Require a small stake locked per identity plus a history of verifiable useful work, so a walnut-sized fake account costs as much to keep alive as a genuine one. Spawning thousands then burns stake and compute, making mass fakery unprofitable while honest agents earn their stake back through good work.
